body:
## Tooling: cross-platform byte/codec reproducibility of the `make verify` surface

Status: **tooling improvement (verification reproducibility)**. Track 85–94 (verification engineering), OS random seed 85. Base commit `91a2094f2e022930069e8cfdc810a3ea1b81cd09`. No new kappa; no mathematical claim, certificate value, patch payload, or the selected frontier changes. Prepared with help from opencode.

### Findings at the base commit (Windows 11, CPython 3.13.15, cp1252)

1. **`ranked-pair-check` crashes**: `research/ranked-pair-verification/verify.py` decoded `lean/CappedMass.lean` / `lean/ConcreteAssembly.lean` with `Path.read_text()` and no `encoding=`, so the locale codec applied (`UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x9d`). The check passed on UTF-8 hosts and crashed elsewhere — an outcome that depended on the host locale.
2. **`machine-transfer-check` crashes**: same root cause in `research/machine-transfer-verification/next-proof/analytic/check.py` (`row_region.count("⟨")` counted 0 against cp1252 mojibake → `Unexpected literal row constructors`). The 240-file package is byte-frozen by its own `publication-manifest.json`, so its sources cannot be edited without invalidating the reviewed publication bytes.
3. **Every regenerated certificate was byte-different**: `scripts/` generators wrote certificates through unpinned text writes, so `'\n'` was translated to `os.linesep`. 39 certificates regenerated by the audited checks differed from their tracked bytes **in every line**, while being equal after newline normalization (39/39 verified). Byte-level receipts (sha256 of a regenerated artifact) diverge from the Linux reference this way.

A static inventory found 7157 locale-dependent text I/O sites repo-wide at the base commit; 150 write sites are in the `scripts/` make surface (recorded in `research/agent-08-verifeng-seed85/evidence/locale-sites.json`).

### Change

- `Makefile`: `export PYTHONUTF8=1` for all recipes. Identical behavior on Linux; this is what lets `machine-transfer-check` pass without touching its publication-frozen sources.
- `research/ranked-pair-verification/verify.py`: explicit `encoding='utf-8'` on its three text reads (not hash-pinned anywhere), so direct invocation also works.
- `scripts/`: `encoding='utf-8', newline='\n'` on **139 text writes across 126 files**, applied mechanically by the committed ast codemod `research/agent-08-verifeng-seed85/pin_text_writes.py --fix` (one keyword pair per call; nothing else changes).
- **27 certificates regenerated**; machine-checked digest-only diffs (see below).
- `tests/test_locale_reproducibility.py`: four regression guards.

### Frozen sources are not touched

The codemod refuses to modify a script named by path in `certificates/selected-result.json`, `certificates/checkpoints/*.json`, or `SELECTED-SOURCE.json` (9 frontier drivers), or whose sha256 appears in a frozen `docs/research/*.json` receipt. The second rule caught three first-pass edits, which were reverted: `scripts/audit_community_candidate.py` (pinned by `docs/research/community-followup-arithmetic.json`, which `audit_followup_candidate.py --check` compares against — the check failed until the revert) and `scripts/verify_frontier617.py` / `verify_frontier617_bindings.py` (tested-source digests in `docs/research/community-cold617-integration.json`). 43 scripts are skipped as frozen in total. `docs/research/preserved-research-manifest.json` records `original_sha256` — bytes as of its historical `base_commit` — and does not freeze current sources.

### Reproduce and verify

    python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_locale_reproducibility.py' -v

Expected: `Ran 4 tests ... OK`. The guards run `ranked-pair-check` under a hostile locale (LC_ALL=C, no UTF-8 mode) and require `PASS ranked pair`; run `machine-transfer-check` the way `make` does (UTF-8 mode pinned) and require `PASS machine-transfer offline checkpoint` plus the Makefile pin; regenerate `certificates/cube-core-family.json` with a real generator (`scripts/audit_cube_cores.py`) and require byte identity; and require `pin_text_writes.py --check` to report `0 unpinned text writes`.

    python3 -B research/agent-08-verifeng-seed85/pin_text_writes.py --check
    python3 -B research/agent-08-verifeng-seed85/locale_inventory.py

### Measured before/after (same host, same inputs)

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `ranked-pair-check` (hostile locale) | exit 1 `UnicodeDecodeError` | exit 0 `PASS ranked pair` (1.3 s) |
| `machine-transfer-check` (`PYTHONUTF8=1`) | exit 1 `Unexpected literal row constructors` | exit 0 `PASS machine-transfer offline checkpoint` |
| Regenerated certificates | 39/39 byte-different (CRLF every line) | 27 changed, **digest-only** diffs (recorded `source_sha256` of edited generators); 0 content, 0 newline differences |
| Isolated test suite | 15-module environmental failing set (recorded at base by PR #921's evidence) | identical 15-module set; no test outcome changed |

Timing evidence for the audited checks is in `research/agent-08-verifeng-seed85/evidence/` (`survey-baseline.json` pre-fix, `survey-after-fix.json` post-fix; `regeneration-receipt.json` records the diff analysis and commands).

### Scope and unresolved obligations

- Only generator text-write keywords, three read call sites, one Makefile export, regenerated source-digest fields, and new tests changed. No certificate value, constraint, kappa, or proof source differs.
- `machine-transfer-check` invoked **directly** (bypassing the Makefile) still fails on non-UTF-8 hosts: its checker sources are frozen by `publication-manifest.json`. `make verify` runs it correctly.
- Residual by design: 14 `open()` calls in `scripts/` with non-literal modes (reported, left alone), the 43 frozen scripts, and `research/`-side package generators, which can still emit CRLF-translated output on Windows. The repo-wide inventory lists the sites.
- Not re-run here (no numpy/sympy/scipy or C++ toolchain on this host): `gen4-bank-verify`, the `frontier741/799-verify` chains, `prime_field_network` and `audit_positive_skip_exact` (compile C++ producers), Lean builds, and the 15 environmental Windows test modules (e.g. `resource` imports). None of their bytes changed.

### Overlap and predecessor work

Surveyed 716 open PRs before submission; none targets locale/codec/newline reproducibility (the closest, #819, makes one gzip artifact portable by a different method on a different object). Concurrent tooling #849/#853/#903/#921 and the earlier #752/#778/#808/#824 accelerate other checks and do not touch these surfaces; PR #921's benchmark evidence supplies the base failing set compared against here (credit: Aaron Wang), and the doctrine follows Maxime Fleury's gzip-container reproducibility audit ("compare canonical payloads across environments"). The repository's verification suite, generators and frozen packages are the predecessors; this change only pins how their text is decoded and encoded.

Prepared for the coordinated research sprint by agent-08, with help from opencode. Apache-2.0. No independent human review is claimed. Finite tooling checks do not discharge the inherited all-size/compiler, hosting, precision/tape and analytic hypotheses, and no full Lean multiplication theorem is claimed.
title: Tooling: cross-platform byte/codec reproducibility of the make verify surface (no new kappa)
